name: Model/Actriz
label: True Panther
lede: Two Berklee kids found a singer at a basement show, lost him to a breakup, and got him back with a bassist who had walked runways in Milan. Dogsbody took Best New Music and a Coachella slot followed.

eras.title: Loud kids, a basement singer
eras.text: Drummer Ruben Radlauer and guitarist Jack Wetmore meet at Berklee in Boston and go looking for a voice. They find Cole Haden at a basement show, and the band they build turns out to be louder than he wants.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Model/Actriz Interview · Crack Magazine: Cover Story · Wikipedia: Model/Actriz
years.h: Two Berklee kids hear a 19-year-old sing and ask him to join
years.p: That was the reaction, as Rolling Stone tells it, when [[Cole Haden|3c6ccacd-8c73-4fe4-88f8-1fef2b5bffe0]] took the stage at a basement show. [[Jack Wetmore|e998aecd-25f4-4737-85e1-182a22e2e193]] and [[Ruben Radlauer|e6fd4e70-2475-4859-b97a-65a287ab3a54]] were shopping for a singer, and they asked him afterward.
years.xp:
Wetmore and Radlauer had known each other since childhood; their fathers played together in an 80s band. Crack Magazine reports they wanted a singer who could handle loud music, and Haden's set was the opposite: long, meandering art-pop songs with spoken word, in the Laurie Anderson mold.

Haden wasn't looking for a band. He told Rolling Stone he was lonely, and after the first rehearsal Radlauer remembered being shocked at how quickly it "sounded like music". Sources differ on the year: Wikipedia says the band formed in 2016, Rolling Stone dates the meeting to 2015.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Model/Actriz Interview · Crack Magazine: Cover Story
years.p: The Boston band had a name as "the cool, scary band", in Aaron Shapiro's phrase to Rolling Stone. [[Cole Haden|3c6ccacd-8c73-4fe4-88f8-1fef2b5bffe0]] ended it anyway, to find what he wanted to say.
years.xp:
Haden told Rolling Stone the heavy-music frame left little room for what he wanted to say. "I needed time away to come back and say the things I wanted to say," he said. Crack Magazine puts the split down to trouble writing material.

Radlauer felt aimless through the two-year gap and joined, in his words, "a million different bands at once."

eras.title: Brooklyn, second try
eras.text: The band reforms in 2019 with a bassist and a new city. Two years of shows, two singles and one cancelled SXSW later, they record their first album.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Model/Actriz Interview · Crack Magazine: Cover Story · Wikipedia: Model/Actriz
years.h: A runway bassist completes the lineup, in Brooklyn
years.p: [[Aaron Shapiro|8625a5e5-8098-4f0b-9b33-2d9c30df64f4]] came from metalcore and had modeled in Milan. Radlauer says he "completed the band".
years.xp:
Shapiro was a Berklee student too. Crack Magazine describes a 6ft 3in bassist with piercing blue eyes and a metalcore past. Rolling Stone puts his age at 28 when the band reformed, and says he had walked runways in Milan for luxury brands.

Wikipedia lists Haden, Wetmore, Shapiro and Radlauer as the lineup from 2019, now based in Brooklyn, and notes Alt Citizen named them a favorite live act that year.

years.p: "Suntan" came out in March 2020 and "Damocles" in June. The band was on the SXSW bill until COVID-19 shut the festival.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Model/Actriz Interview · Wikipedia: Dogsbody (album) · Document Journal: Model/Actriz's Dogsbody
years.h: Summer 2021: Rhode Island, a producer, and a label head from Elsewhere
years.p: The band tracked Dogsbody with [[Seth Manchester|e0e8139c-e211-4810-aa51-68806c74e234]] at Machines with Magnets in Pawtucket.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists Manchester as co-producer with the band. Rolling Stone reports True Panther head Dean Bein signed the band after seeing them at Elsewhere in Brooklyn.

Cole Haden told Document Journal the record is "a portrait of New York", with memories he'd run into again on walks around Brooklyn.

eras.title: Dogsbody, and everyone shows up
eras.text: The debut lands on True Panther, Pitchfork gives it Best New Music, and the rooms go from 40 people to sold out.

years.p: The first single from Dogsbody came out on November 2, 2022, three months ahead of the album.

q: Dogsbody is the perfect foil to Cole Haden's white-hot charisma.
years.src: Wikipedia: Dogsbody (album) · Document Journal: Model/Actriz's Dogsbody
years.h: Pitchfork gives Dogsbody an 8.2 and Best New Music
years.p: The debut came out February 24 on True Panther Sounds. Pitchfork later ranked it No. 33 of 2023; Rolling Stone put it at No. 31.
years.xp:
Jayson Greene's Pitchfork review called the album "the perfect foil" to Haden's charisma. "Crossing Guard" (January 17) and "Amaranth" (February 1) came before release. The record was made with Seth Manchester and runs 37:52.

Haden told Document Journal it's "my life, as a cabaret", and, as Wikipedia quotes him, that he writes as "a gay person working in a genre that's not very outwardly gay". It won Best Heavy Record at the 2024 Libera Awards.

years.cap: Live at Racket, New York, c. 2023
years.src: Rolling Stone: Model/Actriz Interview · Crack Magazine: Cover Story
years.h: Oakland went from "40 or 50 people" to sold out
years.p: Shapiro told Rolling Stone that Oakland, once a room of 40 or 50, sold out on the band's recent tour.
years.xp:
Crack Magazine counts eight months on the road in 2023 and six in 2024. A fan bit Haden's right arm on the Dogsbody tour; he told Crack it "didn't even feel like a malicious bite".

Opening for Interpol at the Beacon Theatre, the venue threatened to cut the power if Haden left the stage.

eras.title: Bigger rooms, bigger names
eras.text: Barcelona calls, Miley Cyrus records a song Haden co-wrote, a second album arrives on Dirty Hit, and the band plays Coachella.

years.cap: Live at TV Eye, Brooklyn, c. 2024
years.p: Primavera Sound booked the band after Dogsbody, and praised them as "pioneers in bringing homoerotic references into a genre as un-homoerotic as post-punk".

years.cap: Radlauer, Shapiro, Haden and Wetmore, February 2025
years.src: Wikipedia: Model/Actriz · Wikipedia: Pirouette (album) · Crack Magazine: Cover Story
years.p: The first Pirouette single, out February 25, 2025, also got the band onto The Late Show.
years.xp: Haden told Crack Magazine the song starts with a five-year-old who wanted a Cinderella birthday party and backed out: "Quiet, alone and devastated." He said he wanted the album to be "the kind of club I wanted to be in."

years.h: Haden co-writes the opener on Miley Cyrus's Something Beautiful
years.p: [[Cole Haden|3c6ccacd-8c73-4fe4-88f8-1fef2b5bffe0]] is credited on "Prelude", the first track on Cyrus's ninth album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pirouette (album) · Crack Magazine: Cover Story
years.p: The second album came out May 2 on True Panther and Dirty Hit, again with Seth Manchester.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists sessions at Machines with Magnets, The Cutting Room and Studio G. Singles were "Cinderella", "Doves" (March 25) and "Diva" (April 21). The Guardian gave it 4 of 5, and Alexis Petridis praised its "thrilling contrasts" between cacophony and control.

Crack Magazine hears a move toward dance-punk and electronics, with Haden describing a "hyper-bright place" and an album that works through his coming-out story. The live show stays confrontational.

years.p: The EP arrived in March 2026, per Wikipedia citing The Fader (March 23).
The band played the festival in April 2026, a month after Swan Songs.
